reason: A flowering shoot is a shoot that bears flowers, so it is the reproductive shoot system. Near-exact match; PO has no 'flowering shoot' synonym.
'Leaves with 2 forms' and 'stamens in 2 forms' count kinds (dimorphism) of the part named before it. 'form' is not itself a structure.
Fragment: the second term of a comparison ('ca. 0.5 × fruit', 'half as long as fruit'). The bearer is the style or beak; the fruit is only the reference.

In Iridaceae the haft is the narrowed lower part of a tepal (the fall or standard). It is expressed as the proximal region of a tepal. This follows the earlier review, which rejected a separate 'claw' class.
A unit of time (how long a flower lasts, chilling hours), not a plant structure.

Fragment: the container of a count ('flowers 2 or 3 in cymule'). The counted bearer is the flower. The container would be cyme inflorescence (PO_0030126, where cymule is a PO synonym) through a container-context rule, not as the bearer.
A quality (how visible something is) applied to lenticels or domatia.
Generic part: it needs the organ it belongs to. Same as the earlier rejections of 'lobule' and 'lateral lobe'.
Narrower: a panicle in a lateral (axillary) position. The position is a property of the bearer and is not needed for grounding.
Exact in meaning: a lateral shoot arises from an axillary bud. PO lists 'axillary branch' as a synonym.

label: floret callus
parent: is_a cardinal organ part (PO_0025001); part_of spikelet (PO_0009051)
definition: A cardinal organ part (PO:0025001) of a grass spikelet (PO:0009051) that is the hardened, often hairy or pointed base of a floret, formed by the base of the lemma (PO:0009037), sometimes with the rachilla joint below it, and that breaks away with the floret.
reason: A distinct, diagnostic structure in every grass treatment (it is hairy or glabrous, has a length, and can be pungent). It is not just the lemma base, and PO has only 'plant callus' (tissue culture). The bare word 'callus' was rejected as generic, so this qualified name is the right handle. Propose upstream to PO.
Generic 'lobe' plus the shape quality 'linear'. The lobe needs the organ it belongs to.
A shape quality; the part follows it ('pairs of linear-lanceolate segments').
Here 'keel' means a ridge on some organ, not the legume keel petal (PO_0025327). As a generic ridge it needs the organ it belongs to.

target: trichome (PO_0000282) on the margin region of the described organ
reason: Setae are bristle-like hairs: 'seta' and 'setae' are synonyms of trichome. Not PO_0030032 seta, which is the moss sporophyte stalk. 'Marginal' maps to the margin region.
Exact: plural of midrib, which is a PO synonym of leaf midvein. This includes the midribs of fern pinnae.
Narrower: a scent-producing floral gland (osmophore). It follows the earlier rule gland → portion of secretory tissue. Lobed and coloured olfactory bodies are scent glands.
Narrower: a flower at anthesis. 'Open' goes to the flowering stage (PO_0007616) context, as 'in the open flower' already does in flora_context_words.
A colour quality of spots or glands.

target: tepal (PO_0009033), member of the outer whorl of the perianth (PO_0009058)
reason: The examples are outer perianth segments. This is a position in a series (outer whorl) of tepals, not a separate class.
A shape quality ('ovoid projection', 'ovoid lobes').
Fragment from a text-extraction error ('pedicel' run into 'later' or similar). The second example is about the stalks of capitula, so even the bearer is unclear.
A quality: pedicellate (PATO_0001438), here of spikelets.
A kind of spikelet (the stalked member of an Andropogoneae pair or triad, as opposed to the sessile one). The whole is qualified rather than given a new class.

Fragment: the container of a count ('seeds 2-5 per cone scale'). This matches the earlier handling of 'per node' and 'per side'. If a container rule is added, cone scale is a PO synonym of megasporophyll (PO_0009027).
Fragment: the container of a count. Same handling as the earlier 'per node' and 'per side'.
A quality. For flowers it is hermaphrodite (PATO_0001340); for stamens ('Stamens 4 perfect') it means fertile (PATO_0000955).
Narrower: a style that is persistent. 'Persistent' is a quality of the style, not part of the bearer name.
Ambiguous without the family. It may be a corona scale (FLOPO_0985020 floral corona), a petal appendage or a staminode. Bare 'appendage' was already rejected as generic.
An adjective of position ('on the petiole') qualifying scales or spines. The structure is the noun after it. Note that 'petiolar gland' is already a synonym of extrafloral nectary (PO_0009057).
